text:
cristina: heads up: after running the new MSI on a Windows build VM, the redwoodctl Windows Service comes up but `redwoodctl localtest --profile=ci` fails with permission denied when reading the profile. CLI works fine interactively. anyone seen the service user not finding AppData?

ryan: which account is the service running as? LocalSystem/NetworkService?

cristina: default from MSI: it created service 'Redwood Localtest' running as NT AUTHORITY\\NetworkService. profile file is in C:\\Users\\ci\\AppData\\Roaming\\redwood\\profiles\\ci.json (accessible to ci user). service logs show access denied.

anita: NetworkService doesn't have access to user profiles. we usually recommend running services as a specific user or using ProgramData. MSI probably wrote user-level profiles during install and service can't reach them.

support-bot: Note: installer v0.10.0 beta writes profiles to %APPDATA% by default. See docs at https://docs.redwood.ai/cli/install#windows for service guidance.

ryan: quick repro command for others:
```
sc query "Redwood Localtest"
# then run as system to emulate
psexec -s -i cmd.exe
set APPDATA
```
you'll see APPDATA points to C:\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile for system services.

cristina: tried running the service as the ci user and it works. but in our CI we prefer a service account. any safe pattern?

anita: two options: 1) have MSI drop a machine-wide fallback at C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles\\ci.json and make CLI check ProgramData when running as service, or 2) create the service under a specific service account and set proper ACLs on the user AppData folder (ugly). Prefer option 1.

infra: agree. ProgramData is better for non-interactive services. but need to secure tokens: use ACLs so only service account can read the token file (icacls + SYSTEM + service account). Also consider using Windows Credential Manager for tokens.

cristina: created a quick hack: after install copy profile to ProgramData and set perms:
```
mkdir "C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood"
copy "%APPDATA%\\redwood\\profiles\\ci.json" "C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles\\ci.json"
icacls "C:\\ProgramData\\Redwood\\profiles\\ci.json" /inheritance:r /grant "NT AUTHORITY\\NetworkService:R"
```
service can now read it. not ideal but unblocks testing.

ryan: filing ISSUE: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/523 - MSI should write a machine-scoped fallback and set sane perms; CLI should check %PROGRAMDATA% when running as service or when %APPDATA% points at systemprofile. adding a unit test for that.

anita: small UX note: CLI error should say "checked %APPDATA% and %PROGRAMDATA%; no readable profiles found" instead of generic permission denied. will include in PR.

support-bot: nightly windows-ci job #322 recorded the same failure earlier; added the hack copy step to unblock until MSI fix.

cristina: thanks all, will keep the workaround in our image and watch the PR. :thumbsup:
